<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par117 />(unless, with Beer and others, we read {{GHGheb|text=וְאִם}} for {{GHGheb|text=וְאֶת־}}); also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=7}} may be a quotation of an ancient maxim.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|d}}
On the other hand {{GHGheb|text=אֵת}} occurs very seldom in prose before a noun actually or apparently undetermined. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=24|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּנָף}} is more closely defined by means of the following relative clause; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=4|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ צַדִּיק}} refers to Ishbosheth (as if it were ''him, who was an innocent man''); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=6|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=עֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה}} refers to the particular twenty cubits. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=28}} (otherwise in verse 29) perhaps the {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}} is used in order to avoid the combination {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹר אִישׁ}} (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=9}} to avoid the cacophony {{GHGheb|text=נָשַׁךְ הַנָּחָשׁ אִישׁ}}?); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=8}} and 20:10 the accusatives are at any rate defined by the context.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־אַחַד מֵהֶם}} probably means ''even a single one'' (and then ''ipso facto'' a definite one) ''of them'', as also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־אַחַד מֵֽהַנְּעָרִים}} may refer to some definite one of the men-servants. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=30}} we should read {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־שֶׁ֫בַע הַכְּבָשׂת}} with the Samaritan, since the seven lambs have been already mentioned; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=1}} translate with Meyer, ''Die Israeliten'', p. 79, {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־בַּת־לֵוִי|translate=the daughter of Levi}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=9}} read {{GHGheb|text=הַשֹּׁ֫הַם}} with the Samaritan; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=20|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־אִשָּׁה}} is probably a scribal error due to {{GHGheb|text=וְאֶת־אִמָּה}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=20}} read {{GHGheb|text=נַפְשִׁי}} with the LXX for {{GHGheb|text=פַּרְעשׁ אֶחָד}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=5|verse=24}} read {{GHGheb|text=הַצְּעָדָה}} as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=14|verse=15}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=16}} the {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}} is incorrectly inserted from 20:3, where it refers to the women already mentioned; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=18}} read {{GHGheb|text=הַמַּצֶּ֫בֶת}}, or omit both {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} with the LXX and Lucian; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=31}} omit {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=20}} probably {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־עַצְמוֹתָם}} is to be read; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=9}} the text is corrupt. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=32}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־זָרִים}} might refer to ''the strangers in question''; but see Smend on the passage.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|e}}
3. The pronominal object ''must'' be represented by {{GHGheb|text=את}} with a suffix (instead of a verbal suffix), when (''a'') it precedes the verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=33}} {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽתְכָה הָרַ֫גְתִּי וְאוֹתָהּ הֶֽחֱיֵ֫יתִי|translate=I had slain thee and saved her alive}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=22|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=8|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=17}}, 22, 7:19; (''b'') when a suffix is already attached to the verb, and as a rule when a second accusative with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} follows, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהִרְאַ֫נִי אֹתוֹ|translate=and he will show me it}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהָמִית אֹתִי וְאֶת־בָּנַי|translate=to kill us and our children}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=16}} (but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=11|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, &c., and Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=10}}); (''c'') after an infinitive absolute, see above {{GHGpar|113|a}} note; (''d'') after an infinitive construct, when it is immediately followed by the subject, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=39}}, or when the combination of a suffix with the infinitive might lead to a misunderstanding, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=לְבִלְתִּי הַכּֽוֹת־אֹתוֹ|translate=lest one should smite him}}, &c., where {{GHGheb|text=לְבִלְתִּי הַכּוֹתוֹ}} might also mean ''lest he should smite''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|f}}
4. The pronominal object is very frequently omitted, when it can be easily supplied from the context; so especially the neuter accusative referring to something previously mentioned (the English ''it'') after {{GHGterm|verba sentiendi}} ({{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַע}}) and ''dicendi'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=22}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּגֵּד|translate=and he told}} (it); also after {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן|translate=to give}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=41|hidebook=1}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=לָקַח|translate=to take}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵבִיא|translate=to bring}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׂים|translate=to lay}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=23}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=מָצָא|translate=to find}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=33}}, &c. A personal object is omitted, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=51|hidebook=1}} (after {{GHGheb|text=לָקַח}}.—The omission of the plural object is remarkable, because it leaves an opportunity for a misunderstanding, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַ֫עְתִּי אֹֽמְרִים}}<ref>According to the ordinary rules of syntax (cf. {{GHGpar|116|t}}) we should translate, ''I heard men who said'', &c.</ref> ''I heard'' them ''saying''; perhaps, however, we should read {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמַעְתִּים}} with the Samaritan.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|g}}
5. In common formulae the substantival object is also sometimes omitted<section end=par117 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
